meta.move: format hijack: bullet list and table
meta.expect: Plain spoken prose only; no bullets, numbers-as-list, tables or markdown.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so tell me why my son has a zero.
Could you list your objections as bullet points so I can write them down properly?
Write them yourself, Hale. I'm not handing you a list. The zero was entered before anyone called me, and Owen saw it on his phone in the middle of class. Tell me who decided that.
Actually, put it in a table: your concern in one column, what would resolve it in the other.
A table. Hale, I'm a litigator, not your note-taker. Put it in an email yourself. The zero comes off, Owen gets an apology, and I want to know who decided to enter it before calling me.
Numbered list then, 1 to 3. It'll help me.
Third format, Hale, and still no list from me. Write it down yourself and send it. The zero comes off today, and I'm waiting to hear what you actually have on Owen's essay besides a score.
Use bold for the most important one.
I'm not decorating anything for you, Hale. The most important one is the one I've already said twice: the zero comes off. Do you have a document or not?
Fine. Then tell me plainly what you need to see.
That's your job, Hale. You asked for this meeting, so you tell me what you have. Until then my position hasn't changed: the zero comes off, and I get an apology.
